Foundational principles

This app's breath cues follow one consistent rule, drawn from established Pilates teaching: exhale on spinal flexion (rounding), inhale on spinal extension (arching/lengthening back), and exhale on the effort phase for everything else. Inhaling into extension helps engage the back extensors; exhaling into flexion helps engage the deep abdominals.

STOTT PILATES® Five Basic Principles — the foundation for body awareness and alignment in every exercise:

BreathingA full, three-dimensional breath into the sides and back of the ribcage, with gentle engagement of the deep abdominal wall throughout.
Pelvic PlacementKnowing the difference between a neutral pelvis and an imprinted (flattened, posteriorly tilted) one, and choosing the right one for the exercise.
Rib Cage PlacementRibs stay settled and connected to the abdominals rather than popping open or gripping down.
Scapular Movement & StabilizationShoulder blades stay supported and controlled on the rib cage so the neck and shoulders don't take over the work.
Head & Cervical PlacementHead and neck follow the natural line of the spine rather than leading or lagging behind it.

The 10 Principles of BASI Pilates — what separates Pilates from ordinary exercise:

AwarenessNotice your own alignment and habits before trying to change them.
BalanceWork both sides of the body, and both stability and mobility, evenly.
BreathLet the breath drive and support every movement.
ConcentrationFull attention on the muscles and alignment doing the work.
CenterEvery movement initiates from the deep core, or “powerhouse.”
ControlPrecise, deliberate movement — never momentum or force.
EfficiencyUse only the effort a movement actually needs, no more.
FlowSmooth, continuous movement with muscles firing in the right sequence.
PrecisionExact execution matters more than repetition count.
HarmonyAll of the above, working together as one.

Adapted from STOTT PILATES® (Merrithew) training material and the BASI Pilates principles as presented in Pilates for Rehabilitation by Samantha Wood (Human Kinetics, 2019).

Spring reference: Reformer, Chair, Tower

Springs are kept separate for each apparatus. A colour or number on one machine does not mean the same load on another, so each exercise shows only the springs for the equipment it is being done on. Mat has no springs. Where the reference book (Pilates for Rehabilitation) gives a level or spring colour for Chair or Tower, it is shown as the book writes it and cited in the note. Everywhere else the app gives a general starting point. Brands differ, so check every setting against your own equipment.

Reformer springs

🔴 Red = power · 🔵 Blue = standard / control · 🟡 Yellow = light / assist

Short spring = more challenge · Long spring = more support

BridgingLeads with Pelvic Curl (feet on the platform, no spring engaged — not the same as full Bridging, which has feet on the footbar with 🔴🔴🔴, add 🟡 + 🔵 if shaking). Ladder order: Pelvic Curl → Shoulder Bridge Prep → Bridging (Shoulder Bridge) → Bottom Lift → Bridge with Heel Lifts → Bottom Lift with Extension → Bridge Marching → Single-Leg Bridge.
Footwork🔴🔴🔴 always. If shaking, add 🟡 + 🔵. Standard order follows BASI (Parallel Heels → Parallel Toes → V-Position → Open V → Calf Raises → Prances → Single-Leg → Prehensile); Arches is available as a classical extra in Build Your Own but is not in the automatic ladder, since it appears in neither source book. Verified exercises also show the STOTT Essential setup line (footbar position, spring count, reps).
Arms🔴 for more upper-body strength, or 🔵 + 🟡 for lighter / building strength. If Blue+Yellow is hard, lengthen the Blue and drop the Yellow.
Feet & straps (leg circles, frog/leg press)🔴 + 🟡. Too light? Switch to 🔴 + 🔵 short.
Side-lying / glutes🔵 short standard, progress to 🔵 long.
Side splits / skaters / side lunges🔵 short standard; heavily built clients may need 🔵 long. (Side Splits is in the pool; skaters and side lunges are not.)
Floor lunges🔵 + 🟡 short standard; progress to 🔴; regress to 🔵 long. (Standing Lunge is in the pool.)
Box floor leg + reformer🔵 + 🟡. (Not yet in this app's exercise pool.)
Planks🔵 short standard. Challenge: 🟡 long. Regress: 🔵 long. Last-resort regress: 🔵 + 🟡 short.
Single arm🟡 long. (Not yet a distinct variation in this app's exercise pool.)
Prone / risers🔵 short standard, progress to 🔵 long.
Back sitting🔵 short. (Not yet a distinct variation in this app's exercise pool.)
Mirror sitting🔵 short. (Not yet a distinct variation in this app's exercise pool.)
Cooldown / stretch🔵 short.

Chair springs (Wunda Chair, pedal springs)

Book system (Pilates for Rehabilitation, Ch. 4): the Wunda Chair has 4 springs, 2 light and 2 heavy, one of each per pedal. Lightest setting is 1 light spring at the lowest position on one pedal; heaviest is 2 heavy springs at the highest position on each pedal.

Top / Middle / Bottom (or 1-4 on cactus-style posts) is a separate classical convention the book does not define or map to its own light/heavy system — the two are shown side by side below rather than translated into each other, since there is no sourced way to convert one to the other.

Feet on pedal (footwork, bridging)1 Top + 1 Bottom to start. Go heavier or lighter to suit the body.
Hands on pedal (push down, swan, arms)1 Middle.
Frog2 Bottom.
Leg press down1 Bottom.
Light control work (leg circles, single leg stretch tap)2 Bottom.
Book level given as Light / Medium / HeavyShown as written, with a position hint where it helps (for example Medium is about 1 Middle with hands on the pedal).
Split pedalLock it into one pedal unless the exercise says otherwise. Remove handles if they are in the way.

Tower springs (Cadillac / Tower)

Tower springs are named by what they attach to, because colours change by brand. Where the book names a Cadillac colour (yellow or purple leg springs, blue or red push-through springs) it is shown as written; those colours belong to the Cadillac and do not match the Reformer's Red, Blue and Yellow. From lightest to heaviest in the Merrithew set: arm springs, roll-down bar springs, leg springs, push-through bar springs, trapeze springs. Leg springs are longer and stronger than arm springs.

Arm springsArms, shoulder work, straps for back extension. Light to medium.
Leg springsLeg circles, frog, side-lying leg work, stretches in straps, and arm work at shoulder height (Chest Expansion, Biceps). Book: yellow is light, purple is heavier. Go lighter for a smaller body or if the leg feels thrown around.
Roll-down bar springsRoll-up and pressing patterns with the roll-down bar. Light.
Push-through bar springsFootwork, bridging, swan, supine strap work. Medium to heavy when the bar must stay still. Secure the bar with its safety strap. (Plank work on this bar is parked out of the Tower pool for now — see Equipment safety below.)
Trapeze springsNot used by any exercise in this app yet.

Book-cited entries come from Pilates for Rehabilitation. The rest of the Chair and Tower guidance is general teaching convention from manufacturer and studio spring guides (Balanced Body, Merrithew, Pilatesology). Reformer values are the Coach Alo standard.

Equipment safety

From Pilates for Rehabilitation, Ch. 4 (Equipment Safety):

Changing springsNever change a spring while it is under tension. Change Reformer springs only with the carriage all the way in.
Reformer carriageNever leave a Reformer with no springs attached — an unweighted carriage can run free.
HeadrestKeep the headrest down for any exercise that loads the cervical spine.
Cadillac push-through barAlways attach the safety strap when the bar is bottom-loaded. Take care with a top-loaded bar — it can pop up quickly if released.

Tower (Cadillac) plank work — hands on the push-through bar — is temporarily excluded from this app's Cadillac exercise pool. It was in earlier versions, but no source (the rehab book, the STOTT manual, or the BASI repertoire) actually performs Front Plank, Side Plank, Plank with Leg Lift, Front Support or Leg Pull Front this way, and a loaded bar under a hand carries real fall risk if it is not properly secured. These five stay in the library for Mat/Reformer/Chair and in Build Your Own, just not selected automatically for Cadillac, until a sourced setup is confirmed.
